title: Ratchet WebView undefined dependencies
summary: Ratchets WebView no-undef warnings by file, rule, and identifier and adds sticky browser fault injection for promoted globals.
reason: An aggregate-only warning budget can silently exchange one undefined dependency for another, while raw property deletion in browser smokes can be undone by namespace promotion.
behavior_before: WebView lint enforced only aggregate counts and browser fault tests removed globals with one-time deletes.
behavior_after: The no-undef budget rejects new or moved file/identifier pairs, and test-only sticky masks continue faulting dependencies after namespace promotion.
manual_validation: GREEN: focused ratchet/mask tests passed (5 tests).
RED: 5 focused ratchet/mask tests failed before implementation (4 failures, 1 error).
git diff --check on all packet paths - PASS (line-ending conversion notices only).
npm run webview:lint:budget - PASS without changing the exact no-undef baseline.
npm run webview:lint:budget:check - PASS (1393/1393 warnings, 0 errors).
npm run webview:lint:budget:check - expected RED on v1 baseline with migration instruction.
npm run webview:lint:no-undef:ratchet - PASS; wrote v2 baseline with 408 no-undef warnings and 250 exact file/identifier pairs.
python -m unittest full WebView tooling checks plus focused sticky-mask support test - PASS (15 tests after v1 migration coverage).
python -m unittest tests.python.tooling.test_webview_tooling_checks plus focused sticky-mask support test - PASS (14 tests).
python -m unittest three converted browser smoke modules - PASS (4 tests).
ruff check on touched Python tests/support - PASS.
FINAL: full browser-smoke support tests passed (11 tests), npm run webview:lint:budget:check passed at 1393/1393 with 0 errors, and the isolated -RequireTests release gate passed.
rollback_plan: Revert the exact no-undef ratchet, its generated baseline, the sticky-mask helper, and the three converted browser fault tests together.
notes:
Existing project globals remain explicit; this change does not broaden the allowlist.
The full browser-smoke support module temporarily reported a concurrent Queue smoke missing the common media no-mutation assertion; the focused sticky-mask test and this packet tests passed.
The v1-to-v2 migration is accepted only by the dedicated ratchet and only when aggregate and per-file warning counts do not increase.
